title: Guide: one program is not enough
description: Guess the deletions and a triangle in one program and demand that the triangle is hit: the answer sets are the deletion sets that hit some triangle, not every triangle. See the guide page "Why a loop".

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% The graph of the guide's figures: ten nodes, fifteen edges.
node(1..10).
edge(1,2). edge(1,3). edge(1,4). edge(2,3). edge(2,4). edge(3,4).
edge(4,5). edge(4,6). edge(5,6). edge(6,7). edge(6,8). edge(7,8).
edge(8,9). edge(8,10). edge(9,10).
fragments.description: The graph. Added to every solver.

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% A candidate: at most k nodes to delete.
{ del(V) : node(V) } k.

% The tempting test: guess a triangle and demand that a deleted node hits it.
3 { q(V) : node(V) } 3.
:- q(U), q(V), U < V, not edge(U,V).
hit :- q(V), del(V).
:- not hit.
#show del/1.
fragments.description: Guesses the deletions and a triangle in one program (wrong on purpose).

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The check sees which nodes are deleted.
glue(del(V)) :- node(V).
fragments.description: The interface atoms: the deleted nodes.

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% No counterexample ever: every candidate is accepted.
#false.

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction    options "--project"
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.block(M)
